result.summary:
Local-SEO and technical-SEO checklist (2025-2026) for the small static site of the Kielce emergency opening and car-key business. It is based on web search results only, because direct page fetching was blocked. Wherever possible I tied claims to Google Search Central pages, but most result text came from secondary summaries of those pages, so exact Google wording is paraphrased. Items marked "unverified" could not be confirmed against a primary source.

The main points:
(1) Town pages are only safe with real local value. Make one strong Kielce set of pages, one "Obszar działania" hub, and a small number (about 5 to 12) of genuinely distinct town pages. Do not build a service × town matrix, because that matches Google's doorway-abuse examples.
(2) Never mark up your own reviews or rating (aggregateRating/Review on your own LocalBusiness). Show "5.0 w Google" as plain text with a link to the Google profile instead.
(3) The FAQ rich result stopped showing in Search around 7 May 2026 (reported by several secondary sources). FAQPage markup is still valid but does nothing visible.
(4) A 24/7 business uses opens 00:00 / closes 23:59 on all seven days. The current build already does this.
(5) Before launch the site has blocking issues. The domain is still a placeholder, so there are no canonicals and sitemap.xml and robots.txt point to twoja-domena.pl. The sitemap stamps every URL with the build date as lastmod. areaServed is a loose text string. The postal code is empty and must be copied from the Google profile, not guessed.

I checked the existing repo at /home/user/psychic-octo-invention/strona-firmy (build.py, dane.json, public/). Repo-specific fixes are included in the relevant findings.

findings.topic: 1. Google doorway-abuse policy: what it covers and why it matters for town pages
findings.detail:
Google's spam policies list 'doorway abuse' as a named spam category. It means pages or sites built to rank for specific, similar queries that lead users to intermediate pages less useful than the final destination. Google's own examples include: (a) several domains or pages aimed at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page; (b) a page listing cities that all link to the same generic content no matter which city is clicked; (c) template pages that differ only by keyword or city permutation.

Secondary sources say the August 2025 spam update targeted doorway pages, and that wording changed from 'doorways' to 'Doorway abuse' in 2025. Possible results are lower rankings or deindexing, for the page or the whole site.

One reported 2026 change, from secondary sources and not verified on the Google page: since 15 May 2026, Google says its spam policies also apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode.

What this means for us: pages like 'Awaryjne otwieranie samochodów {Miasto}', '... mieszkań {Miasto}' and 'Dorabianie kluczy {Miasto}' for 20 towns would be about 60-100 near-identical pages. That is exactly the pattern Google describes.

On competitors: aggregator sites in this niche, such as cenauslug.pl, run hundreds of '...w {Mieście}' template pages. That is a marketplace/price-data model. A one-van local business should not copy it.
findings.confidence: high (definition and examples); medium (2025-2026 update details)

findings.topic: 2. How to build town/area pages safely: how many and what to include
findings.detail:
No Google number exists. What Google signals is uniqueness and real service, not a page count. A Mueller quote reported second-hand (exact date unverified, given as 2019 or 2023): city pages that only catch search traffic without unique value per location are treated as doorways. He also called a plan for about 1,300 city+keyword pages 'doorway pages'. Agency opinions differ: about 10-15 pages (Whitespark) versus about 35 pages tested (Sterling Sky). These are not Google guidance.

Recommended structure for this business:
(a) Kielce is the core. The homepage and the 5 service pages are Kielce-focused, which they already are.
(b) One hub page, 'Obszar działania – Kielce i okolice'. It lists every served town, with an honest typical arrival time from ul. Chodkiewicza 45A, any extra travel charge, a map image, and links to the town pages that exist.
(c) Separate pages only for the towns where real, distinct content can be written. A sensible first set is the Kielce ring and nearby towns: Masłów, Morawica, Sitkówka-Nowiny, Chęciny, Daleszyce, Zagnańsk, Miedziana Góra, Piekoszów, Strawczyn, Górno, Bodzentyn. A second set of larger towns 30-60 km away is optional: Skarżysko-Kamienna, Jędrzejów, Busko-Zdrój, Końskie, Starachowice, Pińczów. Distances and arrival times are unverified; the owner must confirm them.

Each town page needs: a realistic arrival time and route; which services are actually done on site there (e.g. ECU/DPF may need the workshop); real anonymised job examples ('Morawica, Skoda Octavia III, zatrzaśnięte kluczyki, 25 min'); real photos; local specifics (housing estate or apartment-block door types, typical car parc, parking/access notes); local FAQs; a click-to-call button.

Do NOT: build a service × town matrix; swap only the town name in a template; list 30 towns as footer links; target towns the business does not actually serve. Rule of thumb from the guidance: if a page would read the same with another town name pasted in, merge it into the hub.
findings.confidence: high (principle); low-medium (page counts, which are agency opinion; town list and distances are unverified)

findings.topic: 3. Helpful-content, scaled-content-abuse and generative-AI guidance for local pages
findings.detail:
Google's page on using generative AI content says AI is not banned, and can help research and structure original work. But using AI or similar tools to produce many pages without added value for users may violate the scaled content abuse policy.

Scaled content abuse became a named policy in March 2024. It is method-agnostic: AI, human or scraped content all count if the main purpose is ranking manipulation. The Search Quality Rater Guidelines cover it in section 4.6.5 (scaled content abuse) and 4.6.6 (low-effort, low-originality main content).

Reported 2026 changes, secondary and unverified on Google's pages: on about 1 Oct 2026 Google rewrote the accuracy section to stress human fact-checking of AI text. In Sept/Oct 2026 it reportedly added effort/originality criteria and a warning that fake author profiles signal low quality.

'Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content' asks self-assessment questions grouped as Who / How / Why: is it clear who made it, how, and why it exists?

Action items:
- Have the owner review and edit every page, guide articles included.
- Use the real owner or technician name (or the business) as author. No invented personas.
- Use real photos and real job examples.
- Avoid templated AI town pages.
- Keep guide articles (poradnik) genuinely practical, e.g. what to do when keys are locked in the car, PIN-code and immobiliser issues, keyless relay theft. Do not write generic filler.

findings.topic: 4. Title elements (title links)
findings.detail:
Google decides the title link from several sources, but mainly the <title> element and the main visible heading. The <title> text is used for ranking. Problems Google lists: repeated boilerplate across pages, keyword stuffing, and very long titles. Google may drop the site name from the title link if it repeats the site name shown above the result. Google sets no official character limit. The industry habit of about 50-60 characters (about 600 px) is a display-truncation heuristic, not a Google rule.

Pattern for this site:
- Service pages: '<Usługa> Kielce 24h – <krótka nazwa>', e.g. 'Awaryjne otwieranie samochodów Kielce 24h'.
- Town pages: '<Usługa główna> <Miasto> – dojazd z Kielc'.
- Guide pages: the question itself.
- One unique title per page; do not repeat the full 55-character GBP name on every page.

Current repo: titles are 42-68 characters. index.html (65) and uslugi.html (68), which carries the whole long GBP name, may be truncated. Replace that boilerplate suffix with the short brand 'Awaryjne otwieranie 24h' or drop it.

findings.topic: 5. Meta descriptions
findings.detail:
Google's 'Control your snippets' page: there is no length limit on meta descriptions, but snippets are cut to fit the device width. Page content is the main snippet source, and Google 'may' use the meta description when it describes the page better. Google advises a unique, specific description per page, not a keyword list. The common practical target is about 120-160 characters (convention, not a Google rule).

What to include for an emergency service: the service, Kielce and the area, 24/7, the typical arrival time, a non-destructive method ('bezinwazyjnie'), and the phone number.

Current repo: most pages are 96-144 characters, which is fine. Make sure the area hub and town pages each get their own description, not a template with the town swapped. Snippet controls (nosnippet, max-snippet, data-nosnippet) exist but are not needed here.

findings.topic: 6. H1/H2 structure
findings.detail:
Google systems handle multiple H1s (Mueller), and the SEO Starter Guide reportedly says heading order does not matter for Search. A logical hierarchy still helps accessibility and helps Google identify the main visible title, which feeds title links.

Recommendation: one H1 per page that matches the page's intent, close to the <title> but not identical. Then H2s per section.

Service page: H1 'Awaryjne otwieranie samochodów – Kielce i okolice, 24h'. H2s:
- Kiedy dzwonić
- Jak otwieramy (bezinwazyjnie)
- Czas dojazdu i obszar
- Ile kosztuje / od czego zależy cena
- Jakie marki / zamki
- Dokumenty i weryfikacja właściciela
- Najczęstsze pytania
- Powiązane usługi i porady

Town page: H1 '<Usługa> <Miasto> – dojazd z Kielc'. H2s:
- Czas dojazdu do <Miasto>
- Co robimy na miejscu w <Miasto>
- Przykładowe zlecenia
- Pytania

Current repo: every page has exactly one <h1>, which is good.

findings.topic: 7. Internal linking
findings.detail:
Google's link best practices:
- Links must be crawlable <a href> elements.
- Anchor text should be descriptive, reasonably concise and relevant to both pages.
- Image links need descriptive alt text.
- Avoid stuffing too many links.

Hub-and-spoke plan:
- Home links to the 5 service pages, the area hub, the guide and contact.
- Each service page links to 2-4 related guide articles and to the area hub.
- Each guide article links back to its service page with a descriptive anchor, e.g. 'awaryjne otwieranie samochodu w Kielcach', not 'kliknij tutaj'.
- The area hub links to each town page, and each town page links back to the hub and to the relevant service pages.
- Breadcrumbs, already present with BreadcrumbList markup, give a consistent upward path.

Avoid a sitewide footer block of 20-30 town links (spam-like, agency opinion). Put the town list on the hub page. Make sure every page in sitemap.xml can also be reached through internal links (no orphans).

findings.topic: 8. NAP consistency with the Google Business Profile, and GBP name/address compliance
findings.detail:
Name, address and phone must match the GBP exactly on the website (footer, contact page, schema), on Facebook and on directories (panoramafirm.pl, pkt.pl, aleo.com, etc.).

Use:
- Phone: '+48 668 292 270' visible, 'tel:+48668292270' in links, '+48668292270' in schema.
- Address: ul. Chodkiewicza 45A, Kielce, with the postal code taken from the GBP. dane.json 'kod' is empty; it must be filled in, not guessed.

GBP rules (support.google.com/business/answer/3038177): the business name must match how the business is known in the real world (signage, stationery, registration). Adding service keywords or cities to the name is a violation that Google may edit or suspend. The current GBP name 'Awaryjne otwieranie, dorabianie kluczy samochodowych 24h' reads like a descriptive keyword name. The owner should check it matches the registered (CEIDG) or signage name; if it does not, it is a suspension risk. The website must use whatever name ends up on the GBP.

Service-area businesses should hide the address on the GBP if customers are not served there. If customers do come to Chodkiewicza 45A (e.g. for ECU/DPF work), a visible address is correct. Make the website match that choice. P.O. boxes and unstaffed virtual offices are not allowed.

Repo: build.py line 53 puts the long name into schema 'name'. That is consistent with the GBP today; update both together if the GBP name changes.
findings.confidence: high (rules); unverified (whether the current GBP name is the real-world name)

findings.topic: 9. GBP set-up items that affect local rankings: categories, service areas, locksmith risk
findings.detail:
Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. Complete, accurate GBP information improves relevance.

Categories: 1 primary and up to 9 additional, chosen from Google's list (custom categories are not possible). The current primary category 'Mechanik samochodowy' fits ECU/DPF work but under-signals emergency opening and keys. Consider a locksmith category (Polish label likely 'Ślusarz') as primary or additional, and auto-key or ECU-related categories if the Polish list has them. Polish category names are unverified; check in the GBP panel.

Service areas: up to 20 areas (cities, postal codes, administrative areas, not countries or regions), roughly within 2 hours' drive of the base. List Kielce plus the towns actually served, and mirror the same list on the website hub page.

Risk note: locksmiths are a high-spam category. Google Ads requires advanced verification for locksmith services. Third-party sources report that GBP edits in spammy categories can trigger re-verification or suspension. Change name, category or address rarely and only when the change is truthful.
findings.confidence: high (ranking factors, category and area limits); medium (locksmith suspension risk, secondary); unverified (Polish category labels)

findings.topic: 10. Choosing the schema.org LocalBusiness type
findings.detail:
Google's LocalBusiness docs: name and address are the required properties. Recommended: telephone, url, geo, openingHoursSpecification, image, priceRange, and others. Use the most specific subtype available.

Relevant types:
- Locksmith: under HomeAndConstructionBusiness, also listed under ProfessionalService.
- AutoRepair: under AutomotiveBusiness, and more specific than AutomotiveBusiness. It suits ECU/immobiliser/DPF work.

schema.org JSON-LD allows an array of types. Google's documentation does not clearly say how it treats multi-typed LocalBusiness nodes (unverified), but validators accept them.

Recommendation: one sitewide business node with a stable @id (e.g. 'https://<domena>/#firma') and @type ['Locksmith','AutoRepair'], output on every page or at least on home and contact. Other pages (services, articles) point to it by @id as provider/publisher instead of repeating different data. Optionally describe services with makesOffer / hasOfferCatalog (Offer → Service) whose names match the visible service names.

Current repo: build.py line 53 uses ['Locksmith','AutomotiveBusiness']. Switching AutomotiveBusiness to the more specific AutoRepair is a small improvement. Add a 'url', an '@id' and an 'image' (a real photo, e.g. the van or the workshop).
findings.confidence: high (hierarchy, required props); unverified (how Google treats multi-type)

findings.topic: 11. openingHoursSpecification for 24/7
findings.detail:
Google's LocalBusiness documentation: to show a business open 24 hours a day, set opens '00:00' and closes '23:59'. To show a day closed all day, set both to '00:00'. Use a single OpeningHoursSpecification with dayOfWeek listing all seven days.

The current build (build.py line 63) already does exactly this.

The website text ('Czynne całą dobę, 7 dni w tygodniu') and the GBP hours ('Otwarte 24 godziny') must agree. If there are holiday exceptions, set GBP special hours. BrightLocal found that '24 hours' alone does not raise rankings, and a misleading 24h claim can backfire with users and reviews. Only claim it while it is really true.

findings.topic: 12. geo, areaServed, hasMap and sameAs
findings.detail:
geo: Google's examples use GeoCoordinates with decimal latitude/longitude. No precision rule was found (the '5 decimals' rule is unverified). The current geo [50.8489109, 20.6208003] is fine, provided it matches the GBP pin.

areaServed: a schema.org property. It is not a Google rich-result property, and its effect on Google is unverified. It still helps describe a service-area business. Repo issue: build.py line 54 sets it to the string 'Kielce i okolice'. Better: an array of objects such as {"@type":"City","name":"Kielce"}, {"@type":"City","name":"Masłów"}, and so on. It must use the same towns as the visible 'Obszar działania' page and the GBP service areas (Google requires markup to match visible content). A GeoCircle (geoMidpoint plus geoRadius in metres) is an optional extra.

hasMap: build.py line 64 builds a Maps *search* URL from name and address. Prefer the GBP's own place URL (a google.com/maps place or '?cid=' link copied from the profile), so the map points at the verified listing rather than a search.

sameAs: Google's Organization docs list sameAs as recommended (links to other profiles that identify the business). Repo: build.py line 67 uses the share.google short link. Whether Google resolves share.google links in sameAs is unverified, so prefer the full Maps place/CID URL. Add Facebook, panoramafirm or pkt listings, and YouTube/Instagram if they exist.

Also add WebSite markup on the homepage (finding 17).
findings.confidence: medium (Google's use of areaServed/hasMap unverified; schema.org definitions high)

findings.topic: 13. aggregateRating and Review markup: self-serving reviews are not eligible for stars
findings.detail:
Since September 2019, Google does not show review stars for 'self-serving' reviews: reviews of a business placed on that business's own site and marked up with LocalBusiness or Organization (or any subtype). Embedding a third-party review widget counts as the business controlling the reviews, so it is also ineligible. Google's LocalBusiness page mentions reviews only for sites that capture reviews about *other* businesses.

Reported 24 July 2026 update (secondary): a review-snippet guideline banning fake or undisclosed incentivised reviews in content or markup, with manual-action risk for violations.

Action: do NOT add aggregateRating or Review to the business node.

Allowed instead:
- Visible text such as '5.0 ★ w Opiniach Google', updated by hand and accurate, with a link to the GBP reviews.
- Do not copy Google review texts verbatim onto the site as markup. Whether Google Maps terms allow republishing reviews is unverified; the safe default is to link out.
- If testimonials are collected directly from customers with consent, they can appear as plain visible text, never as rating markup.

The current build has no aggregateRating, which is correct; keep it that way.
findings.confidence: high (2019 self-serving rule); medium (July 2026 update details)

findings.topic: 14. Review-growth strategy compliant with Google policy
findings.detail:
Google review policy, as reported by multiple sources (check Google's prohibited-content page before relying on details):
- No incentives (discounts, gifts, free service) for leaving, changing or removing reviews.
- No review gating (asking only happy customers, or pre-screening surveys that send only satisfied people to Google).
- No staff review quotas.
- No pressuring customers on site (shared tablets or kiosks).
- No fake reviews.
Enforcement includes removing reviews and temporarily blocking new reviews or ratings on the profile.

Compliant process:
1. Ask every customer after every job, using the same neutral message (SMS/WhatsApp template), e.g. 'Dziękujemy za skorzystanie z usługi. Jeśli chce Pan/Pani, prosimy o opinię: <link>', with the GBP 'Poproś o opinie' short link.
2. Put a QR code to the review link on the receipt, invoice or business card.
3. Reply to every review, positive or negative, politely and without personal data.
4. On the website, add a 'Zobacz opinie w Google' button (link to GBP) and an optional 'Wystaw opinię' link on the contact page.
5. Mentioning service details in reviews (car make, town) happens naturally and helps relevance. Do not script it.

findings.topic: 15. Current status of FAQ and HowTo rich results
findings.detail:
Timeline:
- August 2023: FAQ rich results limited to well-known government and health sites; HowTo limited to desktop.
- Later: HowTo removed entirely, documentation withdrawn.
- About 7 May 2026, per many secondary sources: Google stopped showing FAQ rich results for all sites. One source dates the documentation notice 9 May.
Google reportedly said FAQPage markup may still be used to understand pages and need not be removed. Unused markup 'does not cause problems for Search'. Search Console FAQ reporting and Rich Results Test support were to be removed in June-August 2026 (completion unverified).

Action: keeping the existing FAQPage JSON-LD (build.py line 71) is harmless. Expect no FAQ rich result. Keep the visible FAQ sections because they answer real user questions, and the markup must match the visible Q&A exactly. Do not add HowTo markup.
findings.confidence: high (2023 changes, official blog); medium-high (May 2026 end date, multiple secondary sources)

findings.topic: 16. Article markup for the guide (poradnik) pages
findings.detail:
Google supports Article, NewsArticle and BlogPosting. No property is strictly required. Recommended properties:
- headline (concise; Google News suggests 110 characters or fewer)
- image (representative of the article, not a logo)
- datePublished and dateModified (ISO 8601 with time zone)
- author (name plus url to a page that identifies the author; use the real person or the Organization)
Google does not guarantee display. Validate with the Rich Results Test.

Use Article/BlogPosting only on guide articles, not on service, town or contact pages.

Repo: build.py lines 410-412 output Article with headline, description, inLanguage, and author/publisher as Organization. Add:
- datePublished/dateModified (real dates, also shown visibly on the page)
- image (a real photo per article)
- mainEntityOfPage (the canonical URL)
- publisher/author pointing to the business @id
If the owner agrees, a named author (e.g. the owner or technician with a short bio on an 'O nas' page) strengthens the Who/How/Why signals. Never invent an author.

findings.topic: 17. Site name (WebSite structured data) and general structured-data rules
findings.detail:
Site names: put WebSite structured data on the homepage (domain root) only, with 'name' (the preferred site name) and optional 'alternateName' (e.g. the short brand 'Awaryjne otwieranie 24h' plus the long GBP name). Keep the same name in og:site_name, the <title> and the homepage heading. The Rich Results Test does not support site names; use the Schema Markup Validator.

General structured-data guidelines:
- Markup must describe content visible on that page (no hidden content, nothing irrelevant or misleading).
- Items should be complete.
- Violations can bring a manual action that removes rich-result eligibility.
Practical consequences:
- Every town in areaServed must appear visibly.
- Every FAQ in FAQPage must be visible.
- Opening hours and phone in markup must equal the visible ones.

Repo: there is no WebSite node yet. Add one to index.html only.

findings.topic: 18. XML sitemap
findings.detail:
Google's sitemap rules:
- Google ignores <priority> and <changefreq>.
- It uses <lastmod> only when it is consistently and verifiably accurate.
- The sitemaps ping endpoint was retired in 2023; submit in Search Console and reference the sitemap in robots.txt.
- List only canonical, indexable URLs that return 200.

Repo issues (build.py lines 476-482):
(a) Every URL gets <lastmod>2026-11-17>, i.e. the build date, so each rebuild marks every page as changed. Google may then ignore lastmod sitewide (secondary source). Fix: use each page's real content-change date, e.g. from git log -1 --format=%cI on its source content file, or a 'zmieniono' field in the content JSON.
(b) All URLs use the placeholder https://twoja-domena.pl. The real domain must be set before deployment.
(c) Make sure 404.html and any noindex pages are not in the sitemap.
After launch: verify the domain property in Google Search Console (and Bing Webmaster Tools), submit sitemap.xml, and use URL Inspection on key pages.

findings.topic: 19. robots.txt, noindex and 404 handling
findings.detail:
Google: robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing. A blocked URL can still be indexed without a snippet. To keep a page out of results, use noindex (meta tag or X-Robots-Tag) or password protection, and do not block that page in robots.txt (Google must crawl it to see the noindex). Do not block CSS/JS, which Google needs for rendering.

For this site, the current robots.txt ('User-agent: * / Allow: / / Sitemap: …') is fine once the domain placeholder is replaced.

Optional: noindex for polityka-prywatnosci.html. It is harmless either way. Hosting must return a real HTTP 404 status for missing URLs while serving 404.html; a 200 status would make it a soft 404. Check this on the chosen host (Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages and shared hosting each handle it differently).

findings.topic: 20. Canonicalisation
findings.detail:
Google: rel=canonical merges signals onto one preferred URL. It is a strong hint; 301 redirects are stronger, and sitemap inclusion is weaker. Do not use robots.txt or the URL removal tool for canonicalisation. The canonical must point to a live 200 URL, not a redirect.

Best practice, widely recommended by secondary sources: an absolute self-referencing canonical in <head> of every indexable page, one per page.

For this static site:
(a) Choose one host (https + non-www or www) and 301-redirect the other variants and http.
(b) Choose one URL style ('/uslugi.html' or '/uslugi/') and use it in links, canonicals, the sitemap and breadcrumbs.
(c) The homepage canonical should be 'https://domena/', not '/index.html'.

Repo: build.py line 146 omits the canonical while 'domena' is a placeholder. Setting the real domain in dane.json is therefore a launch blocker, because without it there are no canonicals and the og:url and BreadcrumbList items are wrong.
findings.confidence: high (Google guidance); medium (self-referencing as a 'Google recommendation', secondary)

findings.topic: 21. Core Web Vitals for a static site
findings.detail:
Current Core Web Vitals and 'good' thresholds, measured at the 75th percentile of real visits, separately for mobile and desktop: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms (INP replaced FID in 2024), CLS ≤ 0.1. 'Poor' starts above LCP 4 s, INP 500 ms, CLS 0.25 (secondary source).

Google: ranking systems use Core Web Vitals, but good scores do not guarantee rankings. Other page-experience aspects do not directly boost ranking. The 'Good page experience' report filter was retired in Nov 2023.

Static-site checklist:
- Inline critical CSS; keep CSS small.
- Preload the hero (LCP) image and do not lazy-load it; use fetchpriority='high'.
- Serve AVIF/WebP with srcset/sizes.
- Set explicit width/height (or aspect-ratio) on all images and embeds to prevent CLS.
- Self-host fonts with font-display: swap and preload, or use system fonts.
- Little or deferred JS; no heavy sliders or chat widgets.
- Use loading='lazy' only below the fold.
- Replace an embedded Google Maps iframe with a static map image or facade that links to the GBP map (web.dev recommends static images or facades for non-interactive map embeds).
- Long cache headers plus a CDN, Brotli/gzip, HTTP/2 or 3.
- Test with PageSpeed Insights and the Search Console CWV report (field data appears once there is traffic).
findings.confidence: high (thresholds and Google statements); medium (poor bounds)

findings.topic: 22. Images and alt text
findings.detail: Google image SEO best practices: - Use real elements (not CSS backgrounds) for meaningful images. - Place images near the related text. - Write descriptive, concise alt text with no keyword stuffing. Google's example runs from empty, to 'puppy', to 'Dalmatian puppy playing fetch'. - Use short, descriptive file names. - Choose a good representative image for og:image and schema 'image'. Alt text supports understanding and accessibility; how much it helps ranking is disputed. For this business: - Use real photos (the service van, key programming tools, a non-destructive door-opening kit, an ECU on the bench, DPF cleaning) rather than stock photos. - File names like 'otwieranie-samochodu-kielce-zestaw-bezinwazyjny.webp' and 'programowanie-kluczyka-toyota.webp'. - Alt text like 'Technik otwiera zatrzaśnięte drzwi samochodu narzędziem bezinwazyjnym' rather than 'otwieranie samochodów Kielce tanio 24h ślusarz'. - Decorative icons get alt="". - Remove EXIF location data if privacy is a concern. It is not a ranking factor (unverified claims say otherwise).

findings.topic: 23. Polish keyword clusters and patterns from strong emergency-locksmith sites (inspiration, not copying)
findings.detail:
Search results were mostly aggregators; direct page fetches were blocked. Patterns below are summarised in my own words.

Patterns common on high-ranking 'pogotowie zamkowe 24h' style pages:
- A large click-to-call phone number above the fold.
- An explicit '24/7' claim and an arrival-time claim.
- Emphasis on non-destructive opening ('bezinwazyjne').
- A price-factors section, often a 'cennik' with price ranges.
- Owner identity verification (a legal or ethical trust signal).
- Lists of districts or towns served.
- Brands, models and lock types handled.
- FAQs.

Aggregator data, approximate and unverified for Kielce specifically:
- National average for emergency standard door opening about 318 zł; Warsaw highest at about 400 zł; Ostrowiec Św. about 282 zł.
- Typical job time 20 min to 2.5 h.
- kb.pl publishes a 2026 key-duplication price list for Kielce; the most expensive item is car keys with rolling-code encoding.

Keyword clusters, one per service page (search volumes unverified):
- Car opening: awaryjne otwieranie samochodów Kielce / otwieranie auta / zatrzaśnięte kluczyki w samochodzie.
- Home opening: awaryjne otwieranie drzwi / mieszkań Kielce / pogotowie zamkowe Kielce / ślusarz Kielce 24h.
- Keys: dorabianie kluczy samochodowych Kielce / kodowanie (programowanie) kluczyków / zgubione wszystkie kluczyki / kluczyk z immobiliserem / pilot do auta / kluczyk keyless.
- ECU: naprawa (programowanie) sterowników ECU Kielce / immobiliser.
- DPF: czyszczenie / regeneracja / diagnostyka DPF Kielce (never 'usuwanie DPF').

Town modifiers come only through the hub and selected town pages (finding 2).
findings.confidence: low-medium (aggregator data and patterns; keyword volumes unverified)

findings.topic: 24. Pre-launch blocker list for this repo (/home/user/psychic-octo-invention/strona-firmy)
findings.detail:
1. Set the real domain in dane.json ('domena' is currently '[https://twoja-domena.pl]'). This turns on canonicals (build.py line 146) and fixes the sitemap and robots URLs (lines 479-482), og:url and the BreadcrumbList URLs.
2. Fill 'kod' (postal code) in dane.json from the GBP. Do not guess.
3. In sitemap generation, replace the build-date lastmod with per-page real modification dates.
4. Change schema areaServed from a string to an array of City objects that match a visible 'Obszar działania' page (create that hub page).
5. Replace hasMap and sameAs with the canonical GBP Maps place URL, and add other real profiles to sameAs.
6. Change @type to ['Locksmith','AutoRepair']; add @id, url, image and (optionally) priceRange.
7. Add a WebSite node (name, alternateName, url) on index.html only.
8. Add datePublished, dateModified and image to Article on the guide pages, and show the dates visibly.
9. Never add aggregateRating or Review for the business; link to the GBP reviews instead.
10. Shorten boilerplate in titles (uslugi.html, index.html).
11. Make sure hosting returns a real 404 status and 301-redirects http and www variants.
12. After deployment: Search Console domain verification, sitemap submission, URL Inspection, and one PageSpeed Insights run per template.
13. Put the website URL on the GBP. Optionally add UTM parameters to tell GBP traffic apart in analytics; this is general practice, and its ranking effect is unverified.

result.summary:
Legal and honesty check for Polish marketing copy for a 24/7 mobile business in Kielce: emergency car, flat and house opening, car keys, ECU/immobilizer work and DPF service. Limitation: the shared web-search budget for this turn ran out after 8 searches. Search results confirmed the main legal framework: the price-display act (art. 4), the art. 7 black list in the unfair market practices act, the uncertain legal status and enforcement of DPF removal plus media reports of 2026 inspection reforms, and art. 306a kk (3 months to 5 years). Several points come from general knowledge of Polish and EU law and were not re-checked this session: exact paragraph numbers, ownership-verification practice, RODO/cookies, the Google review policies and the 'Pogotowie' naming question. Each is marked 'unverified' in its confidence field, and a Polish lawyer should review before publication.

Main conclusions:
(1) Quote a gross (brutto) price before leaving and confirm it on site before starting work. Name every surcharge (travel, night, weekend).
(2) Avoid unprovable superlatives and absolute claims ('najtańszy', 'nr 1', 'zawsze bez uszkodzeń', '100%') and guaranteed arrival times. Under both acts the burden of proof is on the business.
(3) Publishing the ownership-check procedure is safe and builds trust. Opening for someone who is not entitled carries criminal risk (aiding burglary, art. 193 kk, art. 191 §1a kk).
(4) DPF removal makes a vehicle fail the technical conditions for road use. The site should say clearly that the business does not do it. 2025-2026 EU/PL inspection reforms targeting DPF tampering are reported, but their dates were not confirmed.
(5) Never offer or use 'korekta licznika' as a keyword (art. 306a kk). The same caution applies to 'immo off'.
(6) A contact page without cookies still needs an art. 13 RODO notice and business identification data. A cookie banner is not needed only if there are no third-party embeds (Maps iframe, Google Fonts CDN, reCAPTCHA, pixels).
(7) Show Google reviews as a dated link or badge. Do not add self-serving review schema. Omnibus rules require saying whether and how reviews are checked.
(8) No specific legal ban on the word 'Pogotowie' was found (unverified). Avoid suggesting the business is a public emergency service, and do not use competitors' brand names or copy their text.

findings.topic: 1. Price information before the service (informowanie o cenie)
findings.detail:
Ustawa z 9 maja 2014 o informowaniu o cenach towarów i usług (t.j. Dz.U. 2023 poz. 168), art. 4 ust. 1: the price of a service must be shown clearly, unambiguously and in a comparable way at the place where the service is offered. The detailed rules are in the MRiT regulation of 19 Dec 2022 on displaying prices. UOKiK appeal decisions uphold WIIH fines when a price is shown without the scope of the service. Fines found range from hundreds to a few thousand PLN. 'Cena' in this act means the gross price, including VAT. For a mobile service the website and the phone call are effectively the offer. The unfair market practices act (upnpr) art. 6 ust. 4 also treats price incl. taxes, or how it is calculated, plus any extra charges as material information in an 'invitation to purchase'. In practice: give the price, or a binding range with what drives it (car model, type of lock, night or weekend), before leaving. Confirm the final price on site BEFORE starting, preferably on a short written 'zlecenie'.
SAFE: 'Cenę podajemy przez telefon przed wyjazdem i potwierdzamy na miejscu przed rozpoczęciem pracy.' 'Ceny brutto. Dopłata nocna (22:00–6:00): X zł. Dojazd poza Kielce: wg cennika.'
RISKY: 'od 49 zł' when the typical job costs several times more (bait); 'bez ukrytych kosztów' / 'bez dopłat' if night or travel surcharges exist; 'cena do uzgodnienia' with no indication at all.
findings.confidence: High for art. 4 and the gross-price rule (seen in search results). Medium for upnpr art. 6 ust. 4 (from knowledge, unverified this session).

findings.topic: 2. Off-premises consumer contract: information duties and withdrawal (urgent repair exception)
findings.detail:
A job done at the customer's car or door for a consumer is normally an 'umowa zawarta poza lokalem przedsiębiorstwa' under the ustawa o prawach konsumenta (30 May 2014). Before the contract the trader must give its identity, address, price or method of calculating it, and information on the right of withdrawal. The contract must be confirmed on paper or, with consent, on another durable medium. Two withdrawal exceptions matter here: (a) a service fully performed with the consumer's express consent after being told they lose the withdrawal right; (b) the consumer expressly asked the trader to come for an urgent repair or maintenance. Under (b) the right still covers any extra services or goods beyond what was requested. I believe this is art. 38 ust. 1 pkt 1 and pkt 8 after the 2023 renumbering. A simplified-information regime for small urgent repairs also exists (art. 20, value threshold not checked). If withdrawal information is missing, the withdrawal period can extend by 12 months.
PRACTICAL/SAFE: a one-page 'Zlecenie usługi' with the agreed gross price, a tick-box asking for immediate performance and confirming the customer knows the withdrawal right is lost once the work is done, and the customer's signature. Do not sell extras on site (e.g. a new lock cylinder) without separate consent and a price.
findings.confidence: Medium. The framework is well established, but the article/paragraph numbers and the art. 20 threshold are unverified this session.

findings.topic: 3. Black-list practices (art. 7 upnpr) relevant to locksmith / car-key copy
findings.detail:
Art. 7 of the ustawa o przeciwdziałaniu nieuczciwym praktykom rynkowym (t.j. Dz.U. 2023 poz. 845; implements Directive 2005/29/EC) lists practices that are unfair in all circumstances. No proof of effect on consumers is needed. Items most relevant here (numbering from memory, verify):
- displaying certificates, quality marks or trust badges without authorisation ('certyfikowany', 'licencjonowany ślusarz', fake 'Rzetelna Firma' badges). Locksmithing is not a licensed profession in Poland, so 'licencja' claims mislead unless the document is real.
- claiming approval by a public body ('współpracujemy z policją/strażą', 'autoryzowany partner X') unless true and documented.
- false time pressure ('tylko dziś', fake countdowns).
- presenting consumers' statutory rights as a special feature of the offer, e.g. 'U nas masz prawo do reklamacji!'.
- materially inaccurate claims about a security risk to scare the customer (e.g. 'Twój zamek złodziej otworzy w 5 sekund – wymień natychmiast').
- calling something 'gratis'/'bezpłatny'/'darmowy' when the customer pays anything beyond unavoidable costs, e.g. 'darmowy dojazd' that is later added to the bill, or 'bezpłatna wycena' that becomes a 'diagnostic fee'.
- creating the impression that something can be lawfully sold or used when it cannot (relevant to 'DPF off', see finding 11).
UOKiK can impose fines of up to 10% of turnover for practices harming collective consumer interests. Individual consumers can sue under art. 12 upnpr.
findings.confidence: High that art. 7 is the black list (confirmed). Medium on the item numbering and wording, which is unverified.

findings.topic: 4. Superlatives and absolute claims ('najtańszy', 'nr 1', 'zawsze bez uszkodzeń', '100% skuteczności')
findings.detail:
Two acts apply. Under upnpr art. 5, a misleading action is any false or deceptive claim, including about price or results, that can change a typical consumer's decision. Art. 13 upnpr puts the burden of proving that a practice is fair on the trader. The ustawa o zwalczaniu nieuczciwej konkurencji (UZNK) treats misleading advertising as unfair competition (art. 16 ust. 1 pkt 2). Comparative claims must meet art. 16 ust. 3 (objective comparison of verifiable features, including price). Art. 18a shifts the burden of proving claims onto the advertiser, and competitors can sue (art. 18). 'Najtańszy w Kielcach' and 'nr 1' are verifiable factual claims you could not prove without a price survey, so they are risky. 'Zawsze bez uszkodzeń' / '100% bez uszkodzeń' is an absolute promise. Some modern cars, frozen or damaged locks and some door locks cannot be opened non-destructively, so one damaged lock makes the claim false. Vague subjective puffery ('solidnie', 'z pasją') is generally tolerated (doctrine, unverified).
SAFE: 'Stosujemy metody bezinwazyjne – w zdecydowanej większości przypadków otwieramy bez śladów. Jeśli istnieje ryzyko uszkodzenia, mówimy o tym przed rozpoczęciem.' 'Uczciwe, z góry podane ceny.' '5,0 w Google (N opinii, stan na MM.RRRR).'
RISKY: 'najtańszy', 'najlepszy w Kielcach', 'nr 1', 'zawsze', '100%', 'gwarantujemy otwarcie każdego auta', 'każdy zamek'.
findings.confidence: Medium-high for the principles. The specific articles (art. 5, 13 upnpr; art. 16, 18a UZNK) are cited from knowledge and unverified this session.

findings.topic: 5. Arrival times and the '24/7' claim
findings.detail:
A guaranteed arrival time ('Dojazd w 15 minut – gwarantowane', 'Zawsze w 20 min') is a factual promise judged by the typical result. If it is regularly not met (night, traffic, jobs in Morawica, Chęciny, Busko, etc.) it is a misleading action under upnpr art. 5, and a broken promise can also support a contractual claim. '24/7' / '24h' is fine only if the phone is really answered and jobs are really taken at night and on holidays. The Google profile says 24/7, so the site must be consistent.
SAFE: 'Na terenie Kielc zwykle dojeżdżamy w 20–40 minut; dokładny czas podajemy przy zgłoszeniu.' 'Okolice (np. Masłów, Morawica, Sitkówka-Nowiny, Chęciny): czas i koszt dojazdu podajemy telefonicznie.' 'Czynne całą dobę, także w święta.' (only if true)
RISKY: 'gwarantowany dojazd w X min', 'jesteśmy pierwsi na miejscu', or a penalty-style promise ('spóźnienie = usługa gratis') unless you really honour it.
findings.confidence: Medium. This applies the general art. 5 test; no case law specific to locksmith arrival times was found (unverified).

findings.topic: 6. Exploiting the customer's distress (aggressive practices) and price escalation on site
findings.detail:
Upnpr art. 8 covers aggressive practices. Its factors (based on Directive 2005/29/EC art. 9) include exploiting a specific misfortune or circumstance that impairs the consumer's judgement. A locked-out customer at night with a child or dog inside, or stranded on the road, is the classic scenario. The typical complaint about 'pogotowie zamkowe' businesses in Poland is a low price on the phone and a much higher one after the door is open. UOKiK and consumer ombudsmen treat bait pricing and on-site escalation as misleading or aggressive practices. No locksmith-specific UOKiK decision was found in this session.
PRACTICAL/SAFE: write a 'no surprises' rule into the copy and actually follow it: 'Jeśli w trakcie okaże się, że potrzebna jest inna metoda lub wymiana wkładki – przerywamy i podajemy nową cenę; decyzja należy do Ciebie.'
RISKY: phone-only 'od' prices with large on-site increases; refusing to give back keys or car access until an unagreed amount is paid.
findings.confidence: Medium. The art. 8 principle comes from knowledge; the exact Polish paragraph and any locksmith-specific UOKiK decisions are unverified.

findings.topic: 7. Reviews and the Omnibus rules (since 1 Jan 2023)
findings.detail:
The amendment of 1 Dec 2022 (Dz.U. 2022 poz. 2581, implementing the Omnibus Directive 2019/2161) added these to upnpr: (a) when a trader gives access to consumer reviews, it must say whether and how it checks that they come from real customers (material information in art. 6, exact ust. unverified); (b) black-list items (art. 7 pkt 23b–23c, numbering unverified): claiming reviews come from real customers without reasonable checks, and posting, commissioning or distorting fake reviews. 'Distorting' includes showing only positive reviews while implying they are representative, or editing review text. Buying Google reviews or offering a discount for a 5-star review is risky under this rule and also breaks Google policy.
SAFE wording near reviews: 'Poniżej wybrane opinie z naszej wizytówki Google (link). Nie weryfikujemy ich samodzielnie – pochodzą od użytkowników Google.' or, if you only collect reviews from real jobs: 'Prosimy o opinię wyłącznie klientów, którym wykonaliśmy usługę.'
RISKY: 'Wszystkie opinie zweryfikowane' without a real process; 'zadowolonych klientów: 10 000+' without data; testimonials written by the owner.
findings.confidence: High that the Omnibus review rules exist and apply from 2023. Exact point numbers unverified; the planned search on review rules was not run because the search budget ran out.

findings.topic: 8. Showing Google reviews on your own site (copyright, RODO, Google rules, schema)
findings.detail:
(a) Copyright: review text belongs to its author, so copying many reviews verbatim is a grey area. Google's official embeds/APIs and its Business Profile marketing materials are the cleaner route. (b) RODO: a reviewer's full name and photo are personal data, and republishing them is a new processing. Use the first name and initial only ('Marek K.') or get consent. Do not copy reviewer avatars. (c) Google Search: since Sept 2019 'self-serving' reviews that a LocalBusiness/Organization shows about itself on its own site are not eligible for review rich results. Marking up third-party (Google) reviews as your own AggregateRating schema breaks Google's structured-data guidelines and risks a manual action. (d) The headline rating must be dated and accurate: '5,0 ★ w Google – N opinii (stan na 11.2026)' with a link to the profile, updated regularly. Do not show 5.0 permanently if it drops.
SAFE: a dated badge with a link to Google, plus a few short quoted excerpts with initials and dates, unedited. RISKY: invented reviews; scraped reviews with full names and photos; AggregateRating schema built from Google reviews; 'najlepiej oceniany w Kielcach'.
findings.confidence: Medium. The schema/self-serving rule is well known. Google's terms on reproducing review text and the copyright/RODO analysis are unverified this session.

findings.topic: 9. Ownership verification before opening a car or making / programming a key
findings.detail:
No Polish statute specifically requiring locksmiths to check ownership was found (unverified). It is still an essential professional practice, because opening a car or coding a key (especially 'all keys lost') for someone who is not entitled can amount to aiding theft or burglary (pomocnictwo, art. 18 §3 kk with art. 278/279 kk) if the locksmith accepts that possibility. The dowód rejestracyjny is the usual proof of the vehicle's owner or user. Typical procedure: (1) take the caller's details and plate number at booking; (2) on site, check the dowód osobisty against the dowód rejestracyjny, or the vehicle data in the mObywatel app. If the registration document is inside the car, open it and check the documents before handing anything over. (3) Company, leasing or rental car: require written authorisation or a confirmation call. (4) If anything is doubtful, refuse and/or call the police (112). The owner can check the vehicle's history at historiapojazdu.gov.pl, and gov.pl has the 'Sprawdź swój pojazd' service. Do not photocopy or scan ID cards; look and, if needed, note the document number only. Copying IDs is generally seen as excessive under RODO; whether the ID-card act has a specific rule on copying is unverified.
SAFE (and a strong trust signal): 'Bezpieczeństwo: przed otwarciem pojazdu lub wykonaniem klucza sprawdzamy dokument tożsamości i dowód rejestracyjny. Jeśli nie można potwierdzić uprawnień – odmawiamy usługi.'
RISKY: 'otwieramy bez pytań', 'bez dokumentów', 'dorobimy klucz do każdego auta bez formalności'.
findings.confidence: Medium for the practice. The legal basis (art. 18 kk aiding) is from knowledge; no specific statutory duty was found, so that point is unverified.

findings.topic: 10. Opening flats and houses: entitlement, tenant / landlord conflicts, emergencies
findings.detail:
Opening premises for a person who is not entitled risks complicity in art. 193 kk (naruszenie miru domowego) or burglary. Art. 191 §1a kk penalises persistently or significantly obstructing someone's use of the flat they occupy. A landlord who orders a locksmith to open or change locks on a flat an existing tenant occupies, without a court or bailiff (komornik), is a known problem scenario (from knowledge, unverified). Good practice: ask for an ID with the matching address, or a lease, title deed or housing-manager confirmation, or a neighbour's or administrator's confirmation. Refuse landlord-initiated openings of occupied premises. In real emergencies (person unconscious inside, gas, fire) the customer should call 112 first. The police and fire brigade have their own powers and may ask a locksmith to help.
SAFE: 'Otwieramy mieszkania wyłącznie osobom uprawnionym (dowód z adresem, umowa najmu, akt własności lub potwierdzenie zarządcy). Nie otwieramy lokali na zlecenie osób trzecich bez zgody lokatora.' 'W sytuacji zagrożenia życia dzwoń najpierw na 112.'
RISKY: 'otworzymy każde mieszkanie', 'eksmisje / wymiana zamków lokatorom' style offers, or claiming to 'work with the police' unless true.
findings.confidence: Medium. The Kodeks karny text exists at the cited sources, but whether art. 193 and art. 191 §1a apply to this scenario is my own reading, unverified this session.

findings.topic: 11. Legality of DPF removal on road vehicles in Poland
findings.detail:
Removing a DPF/FAP from a road vehicle that was type-approved with one means the vehicle no longer meets the technical conditions for road use. Under Prawo o ruchu drogowym art. 66 the vehicle must be built and maintained so that it does not emit pollutants above the permitted limits. The Ministry of Infrastructure position, as reported, is that removal is a design modification requiring new type-approval testing. Consequences reported: a failed technical inspection if detected, and the police may retain the dowód rejestracyjny. Enforcement is weak. Sejm rejected bills that would add dedicated fines for removal. NIK criticised the government and police for tolerating it. The standard smoke-opacity test (limit about 1.5 m⁻¹) usually does not detect removal. 'DPF off' is still unlawful to drive with, and advertising it as legal would be a black-list practice (implying something can be lawfully used when it cannot). The business does diagnostics, regeneration and cleaning only, which is the safe position and worth saying openly.
SAFE: 'Diagnostyka, regeneracja i czyszczenie DPF/FAP. Nie wycinamy filtrów – auto bez DPF nie spełnia warunków dopuszczenia do ruchu.' RISKY: 'usuwanie DPF', 'DPF off', 'wyprogramowanie DPF', 'legalne wycięcie', 'przejdzie przegląd bez filtra', even as hidden SEO keywords.
findings.confidence: High that a vehicle without its DPF does not meet the technical conditions. Medium on enforcement details; the jakiwniosek source is sponsored content.

findings.topic: 12. 2025-2026 changes to technical inspections regarding DPF
findings.detail:
Polish motoring media in 2026 report a coming inspection reform ('Rewolucja w przeglądach 2026'). The reported content: new EU guidelines will require inspectors to use digital tools to detect DPF tampering, and a vehicle with an illegally removed DPF, blanked EGR or disabled SCR will fail. These are media reports, not confirmed Polish implementing regulations. From knowledge: in April 2025 the European Commission proposed a roadworthiness package revising Directive 2014/45/EU. It includes particle-number (PN) testing for diesels, NOx checks, tamper detection, cross-border odometer data and annual tests for older cars. Its adoption status and Polish transposition dates as of Nov 2026 are UNVERIFIED. Some EU countries (e.g. NL, BE, DE) already use PN testing (from knowledge).
Marketing implication: demand for real DPF repair and cleaning is likely to grow. Keep it honest.
SAFE: 'Przed badaniem technicznym sprawdzimy stan DPF i wykonamy regenerację/czyszczenie, jeśli to konieczne.' RISKY: 'gwarantujemy pozytywny wynik przeglądu', 'nowe przepisy od [date]' with an invented date, or 'obowiązkowe czyszczenie DPF od 2026'.
findings.confidence: Low-medium. The direction of reform is reported by several outlets, but effective dates and the final legal text are unverified.

findings.topic: 13. Odometer tampering: art. 306a kk
findings.detail:
Art. 306a Kodeksu karnego was added in 2019, with related changes from 1 Jan 2020. §1: changing a motor vehicle's odometer reading, or interfering with how it measures, carries 3 months to 5 years in prison. §2: ordering someone else to do it carries the same penalty. Lesser-gravity cases carry milder penalties. A commentary notes a legislative slip that left two versions of the article side by side, so check the current consolidated text. From knowledge, unverified: a legal route exists for odometer repair or replacement. The owner must present the vehicle at a stacja kontroli pojazdów within 14 days, and the mileage set must be the real one. The relevant Prawo o ruchu drogowym article (believed to be art. 81a) and any exemption paragraph in 306a are unverified. Police also record mileage in CEPiK during roadside checks.
Implication for an ECU/immobilizer/key business: never offer 'korekta licznika', 'cofanie licznika' or 'kasowanie przebiegu', and do not use them as SEO keywords. Dashboard or cluster work: only carry over the real mileage, document it, and tell the customer about the 14-day SKP duty.
SAFE: 'Nie wykonujemy korekty liczników.' RISKY: any mileage-related wording such as 'regulacja przebiegu' or 'kalibracja licznika'.
findings.confidence: High for the core offence and penalty (confirmed). The replacement/SKP 14-day rule and its exact provision are unverified.

findings.topic: 14. Immobilizer, ECU and other modification claims
findings.detail:
An immobilizer is mandatory equipment for type approval of passenger cars in the EU (UN R116 / earlier directives). Car insurance (AC) policies often require working anti-theft devices. Advertising 'immo off', 'wyłączanie immobilizera' or 'emulator immo' therefore carries a compliance and liability risk similar to 'DPF off'. ECU remapping that changes emissions or power may affect type-approval compliance (from knowledge, unverified). Legitimate services such as key coding, immobilizer repair, ECU repair and adaptation after replacement, and cloning a module when replacing it with the same type are fine.
SAFE: 'Programowanie kluczy i pilotów, naprawa i adaptacja immobilizera oraz sterowników silnika po wymianie/uszkodzeniu.' RISKY: 'immo off', 'wyłączenie immobilizera', 'usuwanie EGR/AdBlue/DPF', 'chiptuning bez śladów'.
findings.confidence: Low-medium. Not checked by search this session; based on general type-approval knowledge.

findings.topic: 15. RODO for a contact page without cookies
findings.detail: Even with no cookies, the site processes personal data: the phone number or email of anyone who contacts the business, any form data, and the IP addresses in hosting server logs. RODO art. 13 requires an information notice ('Polityka prywatności' / 'Klauzula informacyjna') linked next to the contact data or form. It must state: controller identity (firm name, address, NIP, contact); purposes and legal basis (art. 6(1)(b) steps before a contract at the person's request; art. 6(1)(c) tax/accounting retention for completed jobs; art. 6(1)(f) responding, security and claims); recipients (hosting, email, telephony and accounting providers); any transfers outside the EEA; retention periods; the rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict, port and object; the right to complain to the Prezes UODO; and whether providing data is voluntary. A consent checkbox is NOT needed just to answer an enquiry (consent is the wrong basis). A cookie banner is not required ONLY if nothing is stored on or read from the device. Since 10 Nov 2024 the rule is in Prawo komunikacji elektronicznej (believed art. 399; previously art. 173 Prawo telekomunikacyjne; unverified). Common traps that set cookies or send IPs to third parties: a Google Maps iframe (use a static map image linking to Google Maps), Google Fonts from the Google CDN (self-host them; LG München I, 20 Jan 2022 fined a site over this, from knowledge), reCAPTCHA, YouTube embeds, Meta pixel, chat widgets and analytics. Keep 'tel:' and 'mailto:' links plain.
findings.confidence: Medium-high for the RODO art. 13 content (stable law). PKE article number, its in-force date and the Google Fonts ruling details are unverified this session.

findings.topic: 16. Mandatory business identification and the Google Business Profile name
findings.detail: The ustawa o świadczeniu usług drogą elektroniczną (art. 5) requires a website operator to provide its name or firm, address, email and registration data (CEIDG/KRS, NIP). Prawo przedsiębiorców requires NIP in business communications (exact article unverified). A sole trader's legal firm name must contain their first and last name (Kodeks cywilny art. 43(4)). It may add words describing the activity, e.g. 'Pogotowie Zamkowe Jan Kowalski'. Show the legal firm name and NIP in the footer and contact page, next to any brand name. Google policy, not law: the profile name 'Awaryjne otwieranie, dorabianie kluczy samochodowych 24h' looks keyword-stuffed. Google's GBP guidelines require the real-world business name (signage, documents) and forbid adding keywords or hours. That can cause the profile to be suspended or edited, and competitors can report it. Recommendation: align the GBP name with the real or CEIDG name. If the business really trades under a descriptive brand, use it consistently on signage, the site and invoices.
sources: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 (Google Business Profile guidelines; not retrieved this session)
https://isap.sejm.gov.pl (Kodeks cywilny, ustawa o świadczeniu usług drogą elektroniczną; not retrieved this session)
findings.confidence: Medium. The UŚUDE art. 5 and KC art. 43(4) rules are well known but unverified this session; the GBP naming policy is well known (unverified this session).

findings.topic: 17. Using the word 'Pogotowie' in a name or claims
findings.detail:
No statutory restriction on 'pogotowie' in names such as 'pogotowie zamkowe', 'pogotowie ślusarskie' or 'pogotowie techniczne' was found. These are common generic descriptions (UNVERIFIED: the dedicated search could not be run). General limits apply: (a) KC art. 43(5): a firm name must not mislead; (b) UZNK art. 5: a misleading business designation is unfair competition; (c) upnpr black list: no claim of public authorisation or affiliation. So avoid anything suggesting a public emergency service: words like 'ratownictwo', 'służba ratunkowa', 'oficjalne pogotowie miejskie'; the blue Star of Life or red-cross-style symbols; designs imitating 112, 999 or 997; and 'ratownik' titles (the 'ratownik medyczny' title is protected under the Państwowe Ratownictwo Medyczne act, from knowledge). Also avoid competitors' brand names, e.g. 'Pogotowie Zamkowe Warszawa 24', in your name, domain or ads. They may be trademarks or protected business names (Prawo własności przemysłowej / UZNK art. 5). Check the UPRP trademark database before choosing a domain or brand. Warsaw-specific names are irrelevant for Kielce SEO anyway.
SAFE: 'Pogotowie zamkowe i samochodowe Kielce 24h – [Imię Nazwisko]'. RISKY: 'Miejskie Pogotowie Ratunkowe Zamków', emergency-service imitation, or using a competitor's brand as a keyword.
findings.confidence: Low-medium. No specific prohibition was found, but this was not searched (budget exhausted); the conclusions come from general firm-name and unfair-competition rules.

findings.topic: 18. Inspiration from competitor sites without plagiarism
findings.detail: The user asked to draw on top SEO competitors such as 'pogotowie zamkowe warszawa 24'. Copying their text, structure-specific long passages, photos, graphics or FAQ answers can infringe author's economic rights (ustawa o prawie autorskim i prawach pokrewnych, art. 79 civil claims; art. 115 ust. 1 criminal plagiarism, up to 3 years). It can also be an act of unfair competition (UZNK art. 3 general clause / slavish imitation). Google also treats copied or scraped content as low-value spam. Allowed: using the same topics, keyword themes (e.g. 'otwieranie samochodów Kielce', 'dorabianie kluczy samochodowych Kielce', 'zgubione kluczyki', 'programowanie kluczyków', 'regeneracja DPF Kielce'), page types (service pages, city pages, FAQ, price list) and general layout patterns, all written in original words with your own photos. City or area pages (Kielce, Masłów, Morawica, Sitkówka-Nowiny, Piekoszów, Chęciny, Daleszyce, Zagnańsk, Bodzentyn, etc.) are fine only if you really serve there and each page has real local content. Near-identical swapped-name pages are 'doorway pages' under Google's spam policies.
findings.confidence: Medium. Copyright article numbers and Google spam-policy details come from knowledge (unverified this session).

findings.topic: 19. Guarantees, warranties, insurance and certificates
findings.detail:
A voluntary 'gwarancja' (e.g. '12 miesięcy gwarancji na wykonany klucz/pilot') must follow Kodeks cywilny art. 577 et seq. (content of the guarantee statement, duties of the guarantor; consumer-specific rules updated 2023, unverified). Do not present statutory rights (rękojmia / non-conformity of goods with the contract under the consumer act since 1 Jan 2023) as an extra perk (black list, see finding 3). 'Ubezpieczenie OC' should be claimed only if a policy really covers this work. 'Certyfikaty' should name the actual issuer (e.g. a key-programming tool vendor training) and be available to show.
SAFE: 'Na wykonane klucze i piloty udzielamy X miesięcy gwarancji – warunki na paragonie/fakturze.' 'Posiadamy ubezpieczenie OC działalności.' (only if true). RISKY: 'dożywotnia gwarancja', 'gwarancja satysfakcji albo zwrot pieniędzy' without written terms, 'certyfikowany specjalista' without a named certificate.
findings.confidence: Medium. Kodeks cywilny article details are unverified this session.

findings.topic: 20. Summary: safe vs risky wording
findings.detail:
SAFE (use): 'Awaryjne otwieranie samochodów, mieszkań i domów – Kielce i okolice, całą dobę'; 'Cenę podajemy przed wyjazdem i potwierdzamy przed rozpoczęciem pracy'; 'Ceny brutto, dopłata nocna X zł'; 'Zwykle dojazd 20–40 min w Kielcach'; 'Metody bezinwazyjne – o ryzyku informujemy z góry'; 'Weryfikujemy uprawnienia (dowód osobisty + dowód rejestracyjny)'; 'Dorabianie i programowanie kluczy, także przy utracie wszystkich kluczy'; 'Naprawa i programowanie immobilizera i sterowników'; 'Diagnostyka, regeneracja i czyszczenie DPF – nie wycinamy filtrów'; 'Nie wykonujemy korekty liczników'; '5,0 w Google – N opinii (stan na MM.RRRR)' with a link.
RISKY (avoid): 'najtańszy', 'najlepszy', 'nr 1 w Kielcach', 'zawsze/100% bez uszkodzeń', 'gwarantowany dojazd w 15 min', 'od 49 zł' as bait, 'bez dopłat' if surcharges exist, 'gratis/darmowy' with later charges, 'licencjonowany/certyfikowany/autoryzowany' without proof, 'współpracujemy z policją' unless documented, 'otwieramy bez dokumentów', 'DPF off / usuwanie DPF', 'immo off', 'korekta licznika', fake or edited reviews, AggregateRating schema from Google reviews, competitors' brand names, copied competitor text or photos, Google Maps iframes, Google Fonts CDN or tracking pixels without a consent banner.
findings.confidence: Medium. This synthesises the findings above; items marked unverified there remain unverified. A Polish lawyer should review before publishing.

copy_rules: Original text only. Use competitor sites (including 'pogotowie zamkowe warszawa 24' and the Kielce rivals) for page types, section order and topic coverage. Never take their sentences, FAQ answers, photos or graphics. Before publishing, compare each page with the competitor URLs in the research (n-gram or plagiarism check) and rewrite any overlap longer than a stock phrase.

Never invent prices, arrival times, years in business, job counts, review counts or quotes, licences, certificates, insurance, warranty terms, supported brands, job examples, photos or author personas. If a fact is missing, leave it out or keep a visible [placeholder] that the build flags.

Prices: only owner-supplied gross (brutto) prices with a visible 'stan na MM.RRRR' date. Name every surcharge (noc, święta, dojazd poza Kielce). No 'od 49 zł'-style teasers below the typical real price. No 'bez dopłat' or 'darmowy dojazd' unless literally true. Standard line: 'Cenę podajemy przez telefon przed wyjazdem i potwierdzamy na miejscu przed rozpoczęciem pracy.'
Arrival times: ranges and the word 'zwykle', confirmed by the owner for each zone. Never 'gwarantowany dojazd w X min' or 'zawsze jesteśmy pierwsi'.

24/7: write 'całą dobę' only while the phone is really answered at night, at weekends and on holidays, and keep it consistent with the GBP hours. On town pages and in the hub title, keep '24h' only if night trips to those gminas are confirmed. Otherwise use 'Kielce i okolice – dojazd: Chęciny, Morawica, Masłów'. Keep the honest SMS fallback line.

No superlatives or absolute claims: no 'najtańszy', 'najlepszy', 'nr 1', 'zawsze', '100%', 'każde auto', 'każdy zamek', and no guaranteed 'bez śladów'. Use: 'metody bezinwazyjne – w większości przypadków bez śladów; o ryzyku uszkodzenia mówimy przed rozpoczęciem'.

Ownership check on every opening and key page: 'Przed otwarciem auta lub mieszkania albo wykonaniem kluczyka sprawdzamy dokument tożsamości i dokument uprawniający (dowód rejestracyjny, umowa najmu, akt własności). Jeśli nie da się potwierdzić uprawnień – odmawiamy.' Never write 'bez dokumentów', 'bez pytań' or 'bez formalności'. Do not copy or scan ID cards. Refuse landlord-ordered openings of an occupied flat.
